author: finops-cost-lead (AI practice-lead agent; advises, does not sign off)
note: Five reference scenarios (D12), labelled illustrative. Expected outcomes were written BEFORE any engine exists, by applying the rules in DESIGN.md sections 3, 5, 9 and 10 by hand (a throwaway calculation sheet outside the repository, so the arithmetic is consistent). F3 golden outputs and the F4/F5 gates compare the engine with these. Sources supply shape and published shares only; every other input is a labelled scenario assumption. No source outcome figure is used as an input or benchmark. Money is in each scenario's currency; no FX. Global upper cap reflects the Q11 recommendation; if the owner declines Q11, the upper values revert to 'upperBeforeCap'.

conventions.valueFields: levers and totals are annual run-rate gross unless prefixed net; year 1 applies ASM-FIN-045 ramp

headline.statement: 4 of 8 in-scope capabilities with a target are at or above LTM's default target for a Tier 2 estate (executive mode: 8 capabilities assessed; the rest in the workshop)

topFindings.note: Non-production runs 24/7 (OP-06 = Crawl) on 25-49% of compute
Quantified at zero: coverage (50-74%) already meets the steady share once unscheduled non-production is removed. Action: do not buy further commitments until scheduling lands; re-baseline then

value.confidence: Low (band inputs; scheduled share derived from OP-06)
value.label: Indicative value range (conservative / expected / upper), net of estimated implementation cost: not a savings commitment; evidence validation required.

expected.tolerance: Ratings, gaps, severities and finding IDs must match exactly. Money figures within 1% (rounding) or the difference explained in the F4/F5 review.

reasoning: Tier 2 (4 points) so most targets are Walk; Unit Economics target Crawl.
MP-01 = Run puts Practice Operations above target: the agency has the mandate the case describes.

Usage Optimization: core OP-04 Crawl; idle and scheduling depth answers also Crawl, so Crawl against a Walk target. The value uplift makes it High because the scheduling lever's expected net value is about 8% of spend.

LEV-01 is zero in every case: with coverage at 50-74% and up to half of compute in unscheduled non-production, the uncovered steady-state base is nil. This is the intended conservative behaviour, and the advice ('schedule first, then re-baseline commitments') is the useful output.
Upper case (25.5% of spend) comes from the band corner with 74% compute and 49% non-production; it stays under the 29% cap. Confidence Low because every share is a band.

Need index 36.7: base 16.7 (4 one-level gaps over 8 capabilities) + Tier 2 (10) + expected value at least 5% of spend (10). Band 'Establish foundations now' reads oddly for an agency with a FinOps programme (Q14).
scenarios.plausibilityCheck: The case reports strong Azure growth and a commitment portfolio; a model that finds little further commitment value but material scheduling value is consistent with an estate that has bought reservations before optimising usage. No outcome figure from the case is used.

reasoning: Tier 3 (7 points) so foundational and optimisation targets are Run.

Data Ingestion: core answers Run (UN-01) and Walk (UN-03, core because the estate is hybrid), so core Walk; the data-centre costing depth answer (UN-02 Crawl) lowers it by one level to Crawl. Gap 2 plus the foundation uplift gives Critical. The bank's cloud data is good; its hybrid cost model is not.
Allocation: Walk core, lowered to Crawl by Kubernetes allocation (UN-09 Crawl). Gap 2 plus foundation uplift gives Critical.

Rate Optimization: commitments at Run, Spot practice at Crawl, so Walk (the one-level rule). Without that rule it would read Crawl, which a bank saving over EUR 1M a month on reservations would rightly challenge.
LEV-01 is zero: coverage (75%) already exceeds the steady-state share (70%). Consistent with the source's mature reservations practice.
Value comes from scheduling (LEV-04), Advisor rightsizing and idle evidence (LEV-02, LEV-03) and Kubernetes requests (LEV-07): expected EUR 6.9M gross, 6.2% of Azure spend, well under the 29% cap.
Net: one-off internal effort 30 FTE-months (Tier 3 bands for four levers) at EUR 14,000 = EUR 420k; run cost 20% of that plus EUR 300k tooling = EUR 384k a year.
scenarios.plausibilityCheck: The source reports reservations already optimising spend by over EUR 1M a month; the model correctly finds no further commitment value and puts the opportunity in usage levers and hybrid data. No source figure is used as an input or benchmark.

reasoning: Tier 2 (5 points): Kubernetes, AI and SaaS each add a point to a USD 18M AWS estate.

Allocation: Crawl core lowered to Not yet by Kubernetes allocation (UN-09 Not yet). Gap 2 plus foundation uplift gives Critical: the estate cannot attribute 60% of its compute (cluster spend) to products.
Unit Economics: QV-05 Crawl lowered to Not yet by AI unit cost (QV-07 Not yet); target Crawl at Tier 2, gap 1 Medium.
Usage and Rate Optimization each one level below target; both get the value uplift to High because their linked levers' expected net value exceeds 2% of in-scope spend.

Value is dominated by Kubernetes requests (LEV-07, 35% request utilisation against a 65% target) and Spot (LEV-06, AWS 90% maximum): expected USD 3.8M gross, 21% of AWS spend, under the 29% cap. Expected exceeds half of the capped upper because the upper case removes more base before Spot applies (DESIGN.md 10.1 item 5).
Upper case before cap was USD 7.1M (39% of spend); with the Q11 recommendation it is capped at USD 5.22M (29%) because LEV-04, LEV-06 and LEV-07 rest on client inputs, not evidence.
Net year 1 is small (conservative USD 31k) because most levers ramp slowly (0.25 for LEV-06 and LEV-07) and one-off effort is USD 352k.
scenarios.plausibilityCheck: No single public case supplies these inputs. The profile is checked for internal consistency only, and against Flexera's 29% average self-estimated waste as a ceiling.

reasoning: Tier 3 (7 points), so Run targets on foundations and optimisation; many three-level gaps.

Anomaly Management is Unknown (UN-11 'don't know' with UN-10 Crawl): gap computed as if Not yet (3 against Run), Critical, flagged unconfirmed with 'confirm' as the first action. This is the D5 rule: Unknown counts as risk and never scores better than the lowest answer.
Data Ingestion Not yet: normalisation across AWS, Azure and data centre is absent (UN-03 core for a hybrid, multi-provider estate).

Value: LEV-01 is positive here (coverage 20% against 70% steady-state, even after removing all unscheduled non-production); LEV-04 is the largest lever (all non-production runs 24/7); Advisor and Compute Optimizer rightsizing reduced pro rata for idle and scheduling because the tools do not deduplicate; LEV-09 from measured unused SaaS, ramped by renewals (40% in year 1).
Expected EUR 4.0M gross (17% of public cloud spend including LEV-09; cloud levers alone EUR 3.3M, 14%), under the cap.
LEV-06 tiny (AWS only, 5% tolerant share); Azure Spot not quantified until F2 sources the maximum.
scenarios.plausibilityCheck: Internal consistency only; the profile's breadth (SaaS, licensing, data centre) matches the scope shares State of FinOps 2026 reports.

Coverage under 25% of eligible usage with 50-74% steady compute

reasoning: Tier 1 (1 point): targets Crawl; Unit Economics has no default target, so it creates no finding.
Forecasting Unknown (QV-01): gap 1 against Crawl, Medium, unconfirmed.
Rate Optimization is at target (Crawl: ad hoc purchases) yet LEV-01 is the largest lever: maturity and value are separate, which the report must explain.
Conservative case is the band corner with GBP 1M spend, 25% coverage and 25% non-production: LEV-01 GBP 26k, LEV-04 zero (non-production 0% at that corner).

Upper before cap GBP 2.23M (44.5% of GBP 5M) at the corner with 100% compute, 74% steady and 0% coverage; capped at 29% (GBP 1.45M) under the Q11 recommendation. Without Q11 the upper would be shown uncapped, which is the inflation risk Q11 addresses.
Need index 39.0: base 19.0 (4 one-level gaps over 7 targeted capabilities) + expected value at least 5% of spend (10) + growth at least 20% (10).
Conservative net year 1 is negative (minus GBP 8.7k): small estate, one-off effort counted in full. Shown as is.
scenarios.plausibilityCheck: The expected case (12.7% of the band midpoint) sits below Flexera's 29% average self-estimated waste, as expected for an estate where only two levers can be quantified from executive answers.
